name: CA-15
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Kevin Mullin running with large fundraising edge
Republican challenger Charles Hoelter with no reported fundraising
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~97%
model.rationale: A D+26 district with an incumbent Democrat who has raised over $800,000 against a Republican with no reported fundraising leaves little basis to move from the fundamentals. Markets also price this as a near-certain Democratic hold.
model.watch: Any sign of a serious challenger fundraising surge or unexpected incumbent scandal would be the main thing to watch.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Kevin Mullin, the Democratic incumbent, is running for reelection in a Bay Area district that leans Democratic by 26 points. He advanced to the general election and faces Republican Charles Hoelter, who has reported no fundraising. Mullin has raised about $820,000 and holds a substantial cash advantage, with no meaningful outside spending on either side.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, but the district's strong partisan lean, the incumbency advantage, and the lopsided financial picture all point the same direction. Prediction markets price a Democratic win at roughly 97%. The race is rated Safe Democratic, with the main uncertainty being the wide interval typical of low-information races.
